name: NVIDIA B300 (Blackwell Ultra)
disclaimer: Die and HBM footprints drawn to a common scale (1 unit = 4 mm; estimates where noted). Heights, SM grids, DRAM layer counts and the substrate are illustrative.

components.name: Package substrate
components.desc: Multi-layer organic substrate. Routes power and thousands of signals from the chip to the SXM board through solder balls. Blackwell Ultra raises the per-GPU power ceiling to push the extra NVFP4 throughput and taller HBM stacks.

specs.label: GPU power (TDP)
specs.value: Up to 1,400 W (vs ~1,000 W on B200)

components.name: Interposer (CoWoS-L)
components.desc: TSMC CoWoS-L: local silicon bridges embedded in an organic interposer. Carries the ultra-fine wiring between the dies and the HBM stacks, and lets the package exceed one reticle. Unchanged from B200.

components.name: Die 0
components.desc: One of two reticle-limited Blackwell Ultra dies (TSMC 4NP) — the same compute dies as B200. Holds GPCs/SMs, L2 cache, memory controllers and I/O; software sees both dies as a single GPU. Blackwell Ultra's gains come from the 2nd-gen Transformer Engine, taller HBM stacks and a higher power budget, not a new die.

specs.label: Die size
specs.value: ~26 × 33 mm (reticle-limited; exact size not published; same dies as B200)

components.name: Die 1
components.desc: Second Blackwell Ultra die, identical to die 0.

components.name: NV-HBI die-to-die link
components.desc: NV-High Bandwidth Interface between the two dies. Fast and coherent enough that CUDA code sees one GPU — no code changes needed. Unchanged from B200.

components.name: HBM3e base die
components.desc: Logic base die at the bottom of each HBM stack: the PHY that talks to the memory controller through the interposer.

components.name: HBM3e DRAM layers (12-Hi)
components.desc: Stacked DRAM dies joined by through-silicon vias (TSVs). Blackwell Ultra moves from 8-high to 12-high stacks — 50% more layers per stack, same 8 stacks and same footprint as B200 — to reach 288 GB. LLM decoding is usually bound by this bandwidth: every token re-reads the weights.

specs.label: Bandwidth (per GPU)
specs.value: 8 TB/s — unchanged from B200; the extra capacity comes from taller stacks, not a faster PHY

components.name: HBM3e base die
components.desc: Logic base die at the bottom of each HBM stack.

components.name: HBM3e DRAM layers (12-Hi)
components.desc: Stacked DRAM dies joined by TSVs, feeding die 1. 12-Hi, same as the left-side stacks.

components.name: L2 cache (die 0)
components.desc: Shared L2 cache, coherent across both dies. Buffers data between HBM and all SMs; hot weights and KV cache stay here instead of going back to HBM.

components.name: L2 cache (die 1)
components.desc: Shared L2 cache slice on die 1.

components.name: Memory controllers (die 0)
components.desc: Memory controllers + HBM PHY: turn read/write requests into signals for the 4 HBM stacks next to this die. Same 8,192-bit total interface width as B200; now driving 12-Hi stacks.

components.name: Memory controllers (die 1)
components.desc: Memory controllers + HBM PHY for die 1.

components.name: NVLink 5 / PCIe
components.desc: Off-chip I/O. NVLink 5 connects GPUs through NVSwitch (HGX 8-GPU or GB300 NVL72); PCIe Gen6 connects the host CPU. Same NVLink 5 generation and per-GPU bandwidth as B200.

components.name: NVLink 5 / PCIe
components.desc: Off-chip I/O ports on die 1.

components.name: SMs (die 0)
components.desc: Streaming Multiprocessors — the basic compute unit. Each SM has 4 fifth-generation Tensor Cores (2nd-gen Transformer Engine), Tensor Memory and L1/shared memory. The grid is symbolic: this model does not claim exact SM placement. Click **Open SM** to look inside.

specs.label: SM count
specs.value: 160 across both dies (not individually modeled; symbolic grid)

components.name: SMs (die 0)
components.desc: Streaming Multiprocessors (symbolic grid).

components.name: SMs (die 1)
components.desc: Streaming Multiprocessors (symbolic grid).

components.name: SMs (die 1)
components.desc: Streaming Multiprocessors (symbolic grid).

components.name: L1 / Shared memory
components.desc: Programmable scratchpad shared by the threads of a block. TMA fills it with A/B tiles; Tensor Cores read operands straight from here.

components.name: Tensor Memory (TMEM)
components.desc: Dedicated memory where Tensor Cores keep their accumulators instead of registers. Frees registers for other work and allows larger tiles. Same design as B200.

components.name: Tensor Core (5th gen)
components.desc: Multiplies whole matrix tiles in one `tcgen05.mma` instruction, with FP4/FP6/FP8/BF16 inputs and micro-tensor scaling. The 2nd-gen Transformer Engine's NVFP4 path pushes dense throughput to 15 PFLOPS per GPU, about 1.5x B200's FP4 dense rate. Almost all AI FLOPs happen here.

specs.label: NVFP4 dense (per GPU)
specs.value: 15 PFLOPS (vs 9 PFLOPS FP4 dense on B200)

components.name: Register file
components.desc: Per-thread registers — the fastest storage. One slice per SM sub-partition.

components.name: Warp scheduler + CUDA cores
components.desc: Each cycle picks a ready warp (32 threads) to issue. Scalar CUDA cores (FP32/INT32) run the epilogue: bias, activation, quantization.

components.name: SFU (exp / softmax, 2nd-gen Transformer Engine)
components.desc: New emphasis in Blackwell Ultra: the Special Function Units that compute `exp()` for softmax get 2x the throughput of B200, directly speeding the attention layer — most valuable for long-context reasoning models where softmax over large score matrices is a bottleneck.

specs.label: Attention-layer speedup
specs.value: Up to 2x faster attention-layer compute vs B200, via doubled SFU throughput for exp/softmax

components.name: TMA (Tensor Memory Accelerator)
components.desc: Copies whole multi-dimensional tensor tiles between L2/HBM and shared memory asynchronously, without spending threads.

steps.text: 1. Weights W and activations X sit in HBM3e — now 12-high stacks giving 288 GB per GPU.
2. A memory controller reads the HBM stack attached to its die.
3. If the data lives in the other die's HBM, it crosses NV-HBI at 10 TB/s — invisible to software.
4. Data lands in the shared L2 cache.
5. TMA copies A and B tiles from L2 into shared memory, asynchronously.
6. Tiles sit in shared memory, ready for the Tensor Cores.
7. One thread issues tcgen05.mma: the 4 Tensor Cores multiply the tiles, e.g. in NVFP4 at 15 PFLOPS dense per GPU.
8. Partial sums accumulate in TMEM, not in registers. Steps 5–8 repeat along K.
9. Epilogue: results move TMEM → registers; CUDA cores add bias, apply activation, quantize.
10. For attention layers, the softmax over QK^T scores runs through SFUs that now compute exp() at 2x B200's rate — the 2nd-gen Transformer Engine's attention acceleration.
11. Results go back to HBM via TMA; with tensor parallelism, NVLink all-reduces with other GPUs.
